boat

11279.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters underlined.

Air
11279.explanation: air and heir are both nouns with the same vowel sounds pronounced as /eə/

11280.subject: English Language
11280.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters underlined.

Pleasure
11280.explanation:
pleasure is pronounced as [ˈpleʒə], our area of emphasis is on the ''ea'' sound which goes thus ''e''. 

pliable--- [ˈplʌɪəb(ə)l]

pleat----- [pliːt]

plenary-- [ˈpliːnəri]

jeopardy--- [ˈdʒepədi]. from the list of possible pronunciations above, you can see that only jeopardy [ˈdʒepədi] has the vowel sound ''e'' and it is therefore the correct answer to the question.

11281.subject: English Language
11281.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters underlined.

Thunder

11282.subject: English Language
11282.question_text:
Choose the option that has the same vowel sound as the one represented by the letters underlined.

Tear (noun)

11283.subject: English Language
11283.question_text:
Choose from the options the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined.

Thought
11283.explanation:
Both thought and theater have similar consonant sounds at the beginning. The 'th' is pronounced alike with the tip of the tongue in between the front teeth. Hence we have;

thought: /θɔːt/

theatre: /ˈθɪətə/

11284.subject: English Language
11284.question_text:
Choose from the options the word that has the same consonant sound as the one represented by the underlined.

Caliph

11285.subject: English Language
11285.question_text:
Select the word that has the same pattern of stress as the given word.

Enormous
11285.explanation:
The stress pattern of a word is the way all the syllables are stressed in it. There can be main and secondary stress, or unstressed sounds. 

The word SO-LU-TION has the same stress pattern as E-nor-mous as they are both stressed on the second syllable.

11286.subject: English Language
11286.question_text:
Select the word that has the same pattern of stress as the given word.

Honour

11288.subject: English Language
11288.question_text:
Select the word that has the same pattern of stress as the given word.

Quality
11288.explanation:
Quality is stressed on the first syllable /ˈkwɒlɪti/

A. guarantee  is stressed on the third syllable /ɡar(ə)nˈtiː/

B. accepted  is stressed on the second syllable /əkˈsɛptid/

C. bachelor  is stressed on the first syllable /ˈbatʃələ/

D. related  is stressed on the second syllable /rɪˈleɪt/

11289.subject: English Language
11289.question_text:
Select the word that has the same pattern of stress as the given word.

Education
11289.explanation:
Education -  e-du-CA-tion

A.  Duplicity -  du-PLI-ci-ty

B. Economics  - e-co-NO-mics

C. Elaborate  - E-LA-bo-rate

D. Conjectural - con-JEC-tu-ral

Both education and economics have stress in the third syllable.

11290.subject: English Language
11290.question_text: Identify the word that has the stress on the second syllable.
11290.explanation:
A. reproduce /riːprəˈdjuːs/ - stress is on the third syllable

B. always /ˈɔːlweɪz/ - stress is on the first syllable

C. result /rɪˈzʌlt/- stress is on the second syllable

D. understand /ʌndəˈstand/ - stress is on the third syllable

11294.subject: English Language
11294.question_text: Identify the word that has a different stress pattern from the others.
11294.explanation:
IN-te-gral -  /ˈɪn.tɪ.ɡrəl/ 

IN-ti-mate - /ˈɪn.tɪ.mət/

DIS-course -  /ˈdɪs.kɔːs/ 

ac-CE-le-rate -  /əkˈsel.ə.reɪt/

Words that end with "ate' are stressed on the third syllable from the last.

11299.subject: English Language
11299.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

Without our relentless campaigns we might ....... sure of victory in the race for the National Assembly.
11299.explanation: The complete sentence would be: "Without our relentless campaigns, we might never have been sure of victory in the race for the National Assembly." This option uses the correct auxiliary verbs ("never have been") to convey the meaning that victory in the race for the National Assembly would not have been certain without the relentless campaigns.

11302.subject: English Language
11302.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

To check desertification in the arid zones ...... trees should be planted.
11302.explanation:
In the context of combating desertification in arid zones, the term "drought-resistant" refers to the ability of trees to withstand or survive in dry conditions with minimal water availability. Planting drought-resistant trees is a strategic approach to address the challenges posed by desertification, as these trees can thrive and contribute to ecosystem stability even in regions prone to drought.

Options A, B, and C also relate to the concept of dealing with drought, but "drought-resistant" specifically emphasizes the ability of the trees to resist or endure the effects of drought. Therefore, it is the most suitable option in the given sentence.

11304.subject: English Language
11304.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

I like the character that played the role of a political ....... at the last convention of our party.
11304.explanation: "turncoat" refers to a person who changes their allegiance or political party. In this context, if someone played the role of a political turncoat, it means they portrayed a character who switched sides or changed political affiliations.

11307.subject: English Language
11307.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

The man declared his intention from the -----
11307.explanation:
A. Outset - This refers to the beginning or start of something. In the context of the sentence, "from the outset" implies that the man declared his intention right from the beginning.

B. Inset - An inset typically refers to a smaller section of a larger whole, often used in maps or diagrams. It doesn't fit the context of declaring intention.

C. Onset - This usually refers to the beginning or start of something, similar to "outset." However, "from the onset" isn't as commonly used as "from the outset" in this context.

D. Offset - This means to counterbalance or compensate for something. It doesn't fit the context of declaring intention.

Given the context of declaring intention, "from the outset" is the most appropriate option as it directly implies that the declaration was made from the very beginning or start.

11310.subject: English Language
11310.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

The Team Manager told us that the race could only be won by the .......
11310.explanation: To be swift-footed means  having rapidly moving feet or able to run very quickly

11316.subject: English Language
11316.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

The new school is not provided with .......for science practicals.
11316.explanation:
The correct phrase is "enough equipment." In English, "equipment" is a collective noun, and when referring to more than one item, you use the same form "equipment" without adding an "s" at the end. Therefore, the correct sentence is:

"The new school is not provided with enough equipment for science practicals."

Using "equipments" or any other variations would be grammatically incorrect.

11319.subject: English Language
11319.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

llesa witnessed the largest ..... of writers at any convention in recent times.
11319.explanation:
A. turnaround - This term typically refers to a change in direction or a reversal of a situation. It doesn't fit well in the context of a gathering or convention.

B. turnover - This term is often used in business contexts to refer to the rate at which employees leave a company and are replaced. It doesn't convey the idea of a gathering or attendance.

C. turn-out - This term is commonly used to describe the number of people who attend an event or gathering. In the context of a convention, "turn-out" is the most suitable term to convey the idea of the largest number of writers attending.

D. turn-on - This term usually refers to something that excites or interests someone. It doesn't convey the idea of a gathering or convention.

Therefore, "turn-out" is the most appropriate option as it accurately represents the number of writers present at the convention in Ilesa.

11322.subject: English Language
11322.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

The politicians were ....... by the press.
11322.explanation: It means that the politicians faced criticism or mockery from the press. "Ridiculed" means to mock or make fun of someone.

11326.subject: English Language
11326.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

There are several ........ in the farmyard.
11326.explanation: The use of the premodifier "several" suggests that a plural noun should fill in the gap. "Sheep" is the only plural noun in the option.

11327.subject: English Language
11327.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

Audu fought with his ........ brother.
11327.explanation: When referring to siblings, "elder" is used to indicate the brother or sister who is older in age. While "older" is also a correct term to use in this context, "elder" is more specific when talking about family relationships. "Elder" shows the seniority in age within the family, making it the most appropriate option in this case.

11330.subject: English Language
11330.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

The Dark Continent was an ...... for Africa.
11330.explanation: An "epithet" is a descriptive term or phrase that characterises and identifies a person or thing. In the context of the sentence, "The Dark Continent" is an epithet for Africa. This term has been historically used to describe Africa due to the perceived mystery and unfamiliarity that early European explorers and writers associated with the continent. Therefore, option D, "epithet," is the most fitting choice to complete the sentence.

11332.subject: English Language
11332.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

He arrived ....... to see his family leave for the countryside.
11332.explanation: The phrase "in time" means arriving before an event occurs. He arrived in time to see his family before they left. "late" would mean he missed them entirely. So, the complete sentence should read: "He arrived in time to see his family leave for the countryside."

11333.subject: English Language
11333.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

You can travel on your own, ......?
11333.explanation: "Can't you" is appropriate because it matches the positive form of the statement ("You can travel on your own"). Question tags repeat the sentence's meaning in the opposite form to create a confirmation.

11335.subject: English Language
11335.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

Our culture does not allow one to ........ when an elderly person is speaking.
11335.explanation: To "cut in" means to interrupt someone while they are speaking. Our culture does not allow children to interrupt when an elderly person is speaking. "Cut of" and "cut on" are not phrasal verbs and do not make sense in any context. "Cut off" means to stop the supply of something. E.g. "He cut off the electricity supply until they paid their rent"

11336.subject: English Language
11336.question_text:
Fill the gap with the most appropriate option from the list provided.

Raffle draws, like gambling, often end in a ....... for me.
11336.explanation:
For the sentence, a noun is the most suitable option to fill in the gap because of the article "a" that comes before the gap. Therefore, option B. loss is the answer to the question. 

"Lost" and "loose" are adjectives. "Lost" means unable to find one's way; "loose" means not firmly or tightly put in place. 

"Lose" is a verb which means to cease to have something.

11339.subject: English Language
11339.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

If he were here, it could be more fun.
11339.explanation:
If he were here, it could be more fun

This statement was referring to a third singular person. This means that, the event was fun. But the fun could have been more if that person was present.

''It could'' as used in the statement is a probability. There is no assurance that the presence of that particular person would bring more fun. 

Option A is the correct option. 

He did not show up and so the occasion lacked much fun

 Meaning there was fun, but it wasn't much fun because he wasn't present.

options.text: He did not show up and so the occasion lacked much fun
He was being expected to supply more fun
There was not fun because he was not present
He was expected but did not show up to liven up the occasion

11342.subject: English Language
11342.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

Though he is our elected representative he often takes a rather jaundiced view of our problems.
11342.explanation: The phrase "a rather jaundiced view" means a biased or cynical perspective often stemming from an unfavourable stance. Therefore, option B is the closest in meaning because it shows that the representative holds a negative opinion about the problems faced by the constituents.

options.text: He takes  a rather hazy view of our problems
He takes an unfavourable position concerning our problems
He takes  a rather forceful view of our problems
He takes a sickly view of our problems

11346.subject: English Language
11346.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

When I visited James I only gave him a congratulatory card on account of his promotion.
11346.explanation: The sole action taken during the visit was to give James a congratulatory card.

options.text: The only person I visited was James and nobody else
It was only James that I gave a congratulatory card to
All I gave James when I visited him was a congratulatory card
All I did when I visited James was given him a congratulatory card

11347.subject: English Language
11347.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

The events of last Friday show that there is no love lost between the principal and the Vice-Principal.
11347.explanation: No love lost between two people means that they are not friends, they dislike each other intensely. If there is "no love lost" between two people, they have a strong hatred, hostility or enmity for the other person and make no attempt to conceal it.

11349.subject: English Language
11349.question_text:
Select the option that best explains the information conveyed in the sentence.

The politician's inflammatory remarks were heavily criticised.
11349.explanation: The word "inflammatory" refers to something likely to provoke strong feelings of anger or hostility. Therefore, "provocative" captures this essence well.

options.text: The politican's rude remarks were heavily criticised
The politician's provocative remarks were heavily criticised
The politician's bombastic remarks were heavily criticised
The politician's tribalistic remarks were heavily criticised

11352.subject: English Language
11352.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The Governor told the chief that he was only on a routine tour.
11352.explanation: The term "routine" means something done regularly or as part of a normal procedure. Therefore, A. normal and regular visit is the option that most closely aligns with this meaning.

11354.subject: English Language
11354.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The boy was told that he would need several more pints of blood if he was to survive.
11354.explanation: The word "several" in the context of the sentence indicates an unspecified but relatively large number. It suggests that the boy would need more than just a few pints of blood in order to survive. Option A, "many," is the closest in meaning to "several" as it also implies a large but unspecified quantity.

11356.subject: English Language
11356.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The principal told the teacher to stop browbeating the children.
11356.explanation: The term "browbeating" means to intimidate or bully someone, often through harsh or aggressive words. So, B. bullying is the best choice.

11357.subject: English Language
11357.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

Some actions of the Nigerian youth have alienated them from those who were sympathetic to their cause.
11357.explanation:
A. endeared / kindly: "Endeared" means to make someone fond of or attached to something. It is the opposite of "alienated," which means to be isolated or estranged. So, option A is the opposite in meaning.

B. confronted / ill disposed: "Confronted" means to face or address an issue directly. It does not convey the idea of being isolated or separated, so option B is not the correct choice.

C. separated / opposed: "Separated" is similar in meaning to "alienated," but the second part, "opposed," does not match the idea of being sympathetic. Option C is partially correct in terms of separation but is not a perfect match.

D. estranged / well disposed: "Estranged" is very close in meaning to "alienated," as it implies being emotionally or socially distanced. "Well disposed" means to be favorably inclined or friendly. Option D is the most suitable choice as it captures the idea of separation (estranged) and the initial sympathy (well disposed).

So, the correct answer is D. estranged / well disposed.

11358.subject: English Language
11358.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The essay topic is nebulous.

11360.subject: English Language
11360.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The man was able to persuade his willful and obstinate daughter to follow the career he chose for her.
11360.explanation: In this context, the words "willful" and "obstinate" describe a daughter who is stubborn and resistant to change. Therefore "unyielding and obdurate" is nearest in meaning to this. "Unyielding" means not giving way to pressure and "obdurate" means stubbornly unwilling to change one's opinion or course of action.

11361.subject: English Language
11361.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

Mr. Okon has been described as an eagle-eyed editor.
11361.explanation: The term "eagle-eyed" is used metaphorically to describe someone exceptionally observant, vigilant and detail-oriented. Being an eagle-eyed editor means having a keen ability to spot errors or inconsistencies in written material. The nearest in meaning to "eagle-eyed" is "quick-sighted". It means marked by keen quickly responsive sight. "Clear-sighted" means having a good understanding of a particular subject and the ability to make good judgments about it.

11363.subject: English Language
11363.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

In spite of her grim situation, the young widow smiled dutifully at the visitor's pleasantries.
11363.explanation: In this context, the word "pleasantries" refers to polite or agreeable remarks that are often exchanged during social interactions. Given that the widow is in a "grim situation," the remarks are likely related to her loss and would be considered "condolence messages."

11364.subject: English Language
11364.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

I have always believed that my mother is a very impassioned woman.
11364.explanation: The term "impassioned" means filled with or showing great emotion, enthusiasm or passion. Therefore, "emotional" would be nearest in meaning to "impassioned."

11365.subject: English Language
11365.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The party gathering was thrown into a state of euphoria after the election result was announced.
11365.explanation: The term "euphoria" refers to a state of intense happiness and excitement. While A. pleasure captures a similar sentiment, excitement better conveys the heightened emotional state associated with a significant event like an election result.

11366.subject: English Language
11366.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The family discussed the crime committed and resolved to nail the lie to the counter.
11366.explanation: The expression "nail the lie to the counter" means confronting, exposing or making the lie known. Therefore, option A. expose it publicly is nearest in meaning to the expression.

11367.subject: English Language
11367.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

My father was at the apogee of his career when he was retired.
11367.explanation: The term "apogee" refers to the highest point in the development or progress of something.

11368.subject: English Language
11368.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

Though David's condition is serious, his life is not in immediate danger.
11368.explanation: The word "grave" is synonymous with "serious." Both terms imply a state of being critical or urgent.

11369.subject: English Language
11369.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

That punch by the young boxer proved to be fatal.
11369.explanation: The word "fatal" means something that causes death or is capable of causing death. Therefore, the nearest in meaning to the word is "deadly."

11371.subject: English Language
11371.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The presence of the security men in the area will provide a moment of respite for the residents.
11371.explanation: The phrase "a moment of respite" means a break or a pause from something difficult or unpleasant. This means that the relief provided is temporary.

11375.subject: English Language
11375.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

It is time for all concerned to first pick to pieces the strike action before proffering solutions.
11375.explanation: The phrase "pick to pieces" means to examine something very closely or to "critically analyse" something with the intent of finding faults or understanding its components.

11376.subject: English Language
11376.question_text:
Choose from the options nearest in meaning to the word underlined.

The new ruler is big-hearted in his dealing with people
11376.explanation: The term "big-hearted" is used to describe someone who is generous, kind and compassionate. In the given sentence,  the new ruler is characterised by a generous and kind approach in his dealings with people. Option A, "generous," is the nearest in meaning to  "big-hearted" and is the most appropriate choice in this context.

11378.subject: English Language
11378.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

The teacher announced that the class would be making a fleeting visit to the zoo.
11378.explanation: The word "fleeting" means lasting for a very short time, brief, or transient. The opposite of "fleeting" is something that is long-lasting or enduring. Therefore, option C, "long," is the opposite in meaning. It indicates a visit that is not brief but rather of an extended or prolonged duration. Options A and D are not opposite in meaning, and option B is a synonym for "fleeting."

11380.subject: English Language
11380.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

The project is designed to alleviate poverty in the country.
11380.explanation: The word "alleviate" means to make something less severe or to reduce it—in this case, poverty. Therefore, the opposite would be to make poverty worse or to "exacerbate" it.

11382.subject: English Language
11382.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

Civil engineering is predominantly a male profession.
11382.explanation: In this context, "predominantly" means that something is mainly or primarily characteristic of a certain group—in this case, civil engineering is mainly a male profession. Therefore, the opposite would imply that it is not mainly male or is infrequently associated with males.

11383.subject: English Language
11383.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

The officer said that he knew nothing to the detriment of the applicant.
11383.explanation: In this context, "detriment" means harm or damage that could negatively affect the applicant. Therefore, the opposite of detriment would be something beneficial or advantageous to the applicant.

11385.subject: English Language
11385.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

When the driver applied the brakes, they acted up.
11385.explanation: The phrase "acted up" implies that the brakes malfunctioned or did not perform well. Therefore, the opposite would be that it "responded well."

11387.subject: English Language
11387.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

The striking workers have vowed not to return to work until the decision is rescinded
11387.explanation: The word "rescinded" means to revoke, cancel or take back a decision. Therefore, the opposite of rescinding would be to put a decision into effect or carry it out.

11388.subject: English Language
11388.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

It is rare for a leader and his deputy to see eye to eye.
11388.explanation: The phrase "see eye to eye" means to agree or have a shared perspective on a matter. Therefore, the opposite of this would be to disagree.

11390.subject: English Language
11390.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

Common sense requires that one should be decorous at formal gatherings.
11390.explanation: The word "decorous" means exhibiting proper behaviour, good manners and etiquette, especially in formal settings. Therefore, the opposite of being decorous would be behaving in a manner that is inappropriate or "impolite".

11392.subject: English Language
11392.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

The diminutive figure bounces over the track with unfathomable lightness.
11392.explanation: The word "unfathomable" means something difficult or impossible to understand or measure. It is something that is beyond comprehension. The word "predictable" is the opposite of "unfathomable" because it means something that can be anticipated or is expected and that is straightforward.

11394.subject: English Language
11394.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

I'm not interested in buying that shirt. I think it is overpriced.
11394.explanation: The word "overpriced" means that the price of the shirt is too high relative to its value or quality. The opposite of being overpriced inexpensive or cheap.

11396.subject: English Language
11396.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

Despite his laxity in other matters, Ojo's father drew the line at truancy.
11396.explanation: The phrase "drew the line at" means to set a limit or establish a boundary regarding what is acceptable or permissible. Therefore, the opposite of "drew the line" is to have a lack of such boundaries. A. Favoured means supporting or being lenient towards something is the opposite of setting strict limits. B. rejected means refusing something. C. emphasized means to stress or highlight something. D. ignored means neglecting an issue.

11397.subject: English Language
11397.question_text:
Choose from the options opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

The string was taut.
11397.explanation: The word "taut" means pulled tight or not slack. Therefore, the opposite of taut is "loose," which indicates that something is not tight and has some give or slack.

11398.subject: English Language
11398.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word underlined.

Hypertension is a debilitating disease that everyone should prevent.
11398.explanation: The word "debilitating" suggests weakening or impairing, so the opposite in meaning would be an energizing

11400.subject: English Language
11400.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word or phrase underlined.

The Permanent Secretary left his job under a cloud.
11400.explanation: The phrase "under a cloud" means to be in a state of suspicion, disfavour or disgrace as a result of negative circumstances or controversy. Therefore, the opposite of this phrase would be "with a clear record," which means that the person left without any negative implications or suspicion.

11402.subject: English Language
11402.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word or phrase.

We intend to make the reception a diurnal event.
11402.explanation: The word "diurnal" means occurring during the daytime or happening every day. Therefore, the opposite meaning would refer to something that happens at night.

11403.subject: English Language
11403.question_text:
Choose the option opposite in meaning to the underlined word or phrase.

It is surprising that this politician has now turned renegade.
11403.explanation: A "renegade" is someone who betrays or rebels against an organization, cause or principle. Such a person is disloyal to such organisation, cause or principle. Therefore, the opposite of "renegade" would be someone loyal, as they would remain faithful to their commitments or beliefs.

15078.subject: English Language
15078.question_text: The writer uses 'numbed sensitivity' to refer to
15078.explanation: The phrase "numbed sensitivity" refers to a diminished emotional response or a deadening of the ability to feel or react appropriately to violence due to its frequent portrayal in media. This suggests that constant exposure to violent acts in films and television can desensitise viewers and make violence seem less shocking.

options.text: deadening of the capacity to feel
heartlessness on the part of actors

15079.subject: English Language
15079.question_text: What will actually be proved 'if the premise of education is granted'?
15079.explanation: The premise of education in the passage is that good models influence the young. From this, the author builds an argument to suggest what this premise implies—that bad models (like violence on TV) can negatively influence behaviour. Given this, the correct interpretation of what the premise proves in the context of the passage is that violence on television encourages violence in real life. This conclusion is drawn because if good models positively influence the young (the premise), then bad models, such as fantasized violence, likely have a harmful impact, including encouraging violence in real life.

options.text: entertainment on television is harmful to society
violence on television encourges violence in real life
good models can infuence the young
the viewer of fastasized violence is the criminal who acts out violence

15080.explanation: The passage states that "The chance that a black male between the ages of 15 and 19 will be killed by a gun has almost tripled since 1985". This indicates that the number of deaths among this group has significantly increased.

15081.explanation: The phrase "the firearms figures are rising" means that the number of teenagers killed by firearms is increasing over time. The passage paints a picture of a troubling trend in firearm-related deaths among teenagers and suggests that there are more deaths now compared to previous years.

options.text: more teenagers are now getting killed by firearms than by motor vehicle accidents
firearms now have figures that are terribly high
more teenagers now carry firearm than used to be the case

15082.subject: English Language
15082.question_text: In secretary Donna Shalala's view, the situation depicted by the statistics is
15082.explanation: The passage cites Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala's description of the statistics regarding teenage gun deaths as "frightening and intolerable." This is a strong emotional response to the statistics and indicates that the situation is both alarming (causing fear or concern) and unbearable (something that is too painful or distressing to accept).

15083.subject: English Language
15083.question_text: Which of the following statements can be implied from the passage?
15083.explanation: The passage discusses the complexities and puzzling observations regarding the common cold, particularly its transmission and infection theory. It mentions that despite some studies indicating that colds can spread, there are observations (such as those made by the investigator in Holland) that do not fit with the theory of infection. This suggests that the origin of colds and how they spread is not definitively understood.

the origin of colds is inconclusive
people catch more colds in warm weather
people catch colds equally in warm and cold weather

15084.subject: English Language
15084.question_text: A rare disease can be more easily dealt with than the common cold because
15084.explanation: The passage states that rare diseases are easier to handle compared to common illnesses like the cold because there are not many cases of rare diseases, and all of them have been intensively studied. This suggests that there is a greater amount of research and information available regarding rare diseases, making it easier to understand and deal with them compared to common colds, which are widespread and less understood.

people easily develop resistance to the common cold
adequate research exists to uncover facts about such rare diseases

15085.subject: English Language
15085.question_text: According to the writer, some widely held beliefs about the common cold are
15085.explanation: The writer mentions that “some widely held beliefs about the common cold have turned out not to be true,” implying that there are widely held beliefs about the common cold that are not true, or are mistaken (fallacious).

15086.subject: English Language
15086.question_text: From the information in the passage, there is evidence
15086.explanation: The passage provides evidence supporting that the common cold is indeed infectious, especially in the part describing the experiment at the Common Cold Research Unit in Salisbury. Here, a group was inoculated with secretions from cold sufferers, and seventy-three of them developed colds, as opposed to only one person from the salt-water group. This result supports the idea that the common cold is infectious.

15092.subject: English Language
15092.question_text: The expression ''not in memory but in expectation'' as used in the passage implies
15092.explanation: The phrase "not in memory but in expectation" means that young people focus more on looking forward to the future than reflecting on past experiences. This portrays their lack of extensive life experience or accumulated memories—qualities often associated with innocence. They are less rooted in past knowledge or caution and are more open and hopeful for what lies ahead.

15093.subject: English Language
15093.question_text: The statement 'nature warms their blood as though with excess of wine', as used in the text means
15093.explanation: The statement "nature warms their blood as though with an excess of wine" is a metaphor for young men's temperament. The metaphor is saying that young men's temperament is passionate and intense, similar to the way one might act with confidence or enthusiasm after consuming excess wine, which can make a person more animated and assertive.

This suggests that, like a sick person’s sudden but brief cravings, young men experience strong emotions that are intense while they last but quickly fade. 15096.subject: English Language
15096.question_text: The writer says that young people are optimistic in their dealings with people because they are
15096.explanation: The passage explains that young people "trust others readily because they have not yet been cheated." This suggests that they tend to be overly trusting or optimistic without caution, making "reckless" the best choice among the options. Their "courage" or confidence is the result of their optimism and not the cause. This is explained explicitly in the last two sentences of the passage.

15097.subject: English Language
15097.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 16 in the above passage
15097.explanation: The sentence describes the Senate as a body that makes laws, which is a legislative function. "Executive" and "administrative" refer to those who enforce laws, and "judicial" refers to those who interpret laws.

15098.subject: English Language
15098.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 17 in the above passage
15098.explanation: The sentence implies the Senate’s intention to counteract or cancel the president's executive action. This makes "nullify" (to make legally void) the best fit.

15099.subject: English Language
15099.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 18 in the above passage
15099.explanation: The term "arm" is commonly used to refer to branches of government, such as the executive, legislative and judicial arms, so it’s appropriate to refer to the Senate as an arm of the National Assembly.

15100.subject: English Language
15100.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 19 in the above passage
15100.explanation: Within the National Assembly, the House of Representatives could hold an opposing view. "National Assembly" includes both houses i.e the Senate and House of Representatives. They are meant to work hand in hand, but often they can take a "diametrically opposed" viewpoint to that of the Senate.

15101.subject: English Language
15101.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 20 in the above passage
15101.explanation: A Plaintiff is the party initiating a complaint or accusation in a legal dispute. In the passage, the Senate is described as both initiating an action against the executive and judging it.

15103.subject: English Language
15103.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 21 in the above passage
15103.explanation: The primary role of the Senate is to enact (create or pass) laws, making this the best answer over “create” or “compose,” which are less formal in this legislative context.

15104.subject: English Language
15104.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 22 in the above passage
15104.explanation: "Power" is the clearest term to use in the context of governmental authority. The Senate has no authority (or power) to direct the president’s actions.

15106.subject: English Language
15106.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 23 in the above passage
15106.explanation: The president has executive powers. This power is what allows him to enforce and carry out the law.

15107.subject: English Language
15107.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 24 in the above passage
15107.explanation: Regulated is the best option because it means controlling or supervising according to rules. It means that the President's powers might be subject to oversight.

15108.subject: English Language
15108.question_text: Select the correct option for the space numbered 25 in the above passage
15108.explanation: The most formal way to adjust presidential powers in law is through an act of the National Assembly.
